source_caption:
When 17-year-old high school student Christopher Mintz-Plasse was cast in the iconic role of Fogell (aka “McLovin”), his underage status created a highly awkward situation during production. Because California child labor laws rigidly require a parent or legal guardian to be present on set for minor actors at all times, Mintz-Plasse’s mother had to be physically present in the room while he filmed his hilariously messy, R-rated sex scene with co-star Aviva Baumann. Seth Rogen later joked that it was one of the most painfully uncomfortable days of filming, with Mintz-Plasse’s mom standing just inches off-camera watching her teenage son enthusiastically pretend to lose his virginity.

Superbad (2007), directed by Greg Mottola, starring Jonah Hill, Michael Cera, Christopher Mintz-Plasse, Seth Rogen, Bill Hader. Two highly codependent high school seniors are forced to deal with their impending separation as they embark on a chaotic, alcohol-fueled quest to score booze for a massive party and finally lose their virginity before graduation.

source_details.synopsis: Superbad is a 2007 American coming-of-age teen buddy comedy film directed by Greg Mottola, written by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg, and produced by Judd Apatow. It stars Jonah Hill and Michael Cera as Seth and Evan, two teenagers about to graduate from high school. Before graduating, the boys want to party and lose their virginity, but their plan proves harder than expected. Christopher Mintz-Plasse (in his film debut), Rogen, Bill Hader, Martha MacIsaac, and Emma Stone (in her film debut) provide supporting roles. Rogen and Goldberg wrote the script during their teenage years. It is loosely based on their experience in Grade 12 at Point Grey Secondary School in Vancouver during the 1990s. T
